title: Bernstein Upgrades Takeda Pharmaceutical (TAK) to Outperform
content:
Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited (NYSE:TAK) is one of the 10 Stocks to Buy on a Pullback.

On April 8, 2026, Bernstein upgraded Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited (NYSE:TAK) to Outperform from Market Perform and raised its price target to ¥6,900 from ¥5,100, citing “bold” cost-cutting measures and a series of upcoming pipeline catalysts that could help de-risk the business.

On April 5, 2026, Denali Therapeutics announced that Takeda had decided to terminate their collaboration to co-develop and commercialize DNL593, an investigational progranulin replacement therapy for frontotemporal dementia. The decision was based on strategic considerations rather than safety or efficacy concerns, with Denali regaining full control of the program and its intellectual property.

Earlier, Axsome Therapeutics entered into an agreement with Takeda to acquire exclusive global rights to TAK-063, a selective phosphodiesterase 10A inhibitor. The asset will be developed for schizophrenia and Tourette syndrome, with Phase 3-enabling activities expected to begin in 2026. Under the deal, Takeda received an upfront payment and remains eligible for milestone payments and royalties tied to future development and commercialization.Bernstein Upgrades Takeda Pharmaceutical (TAK) to Outperform

Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited (NYSE:TAK) is a global biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing treatments across multiple therapeutic areas.

title: Is Axsome Therapeutics (AXSM) Still Attractively Priced After Its 72% One-Year Surge

If you are wondering whether Axsome Therapeutics at around US$178 per share still offers value, you are not alone in asking what the current price really reflects. The stock has seen a 4.9% return over the last week and 14.1% over the last 30 days, while year to date it is close to flat with a 0.3% decline. The 1 year return sits at 72.0% and the 3 year and 5 year returns are 152.8% and 243.0% respectively. Recent coverage has highlighted Axsome Therapeutics as a key name in the Pharmaceuticals and Biotech space, with attention on how its late stage pipeline and commercial portfolio are being valued by the market. That context helps explain why sentiment and trading activity have been in focus for investors watching the stock. On Simply Wall St's valuation checks, Axsome Therapeutics scores 4 out of 6. This raises an important question about what traditional valuation models are missing and how a more complete framework later in this article might give you a clearer view of what you are really paying for.

Approach 1: Axsome Therapeutics Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Analysis

A Discounted Cash Flow, or DCF, model estimates what a business could be worth by projecting its future cash flows and discounting them back to today, using a required rate of return.

For Axsome Therapeutics, the model used is a 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity approach, based on cash flow projections in US$. The latest twelve month free cash flow is a loss of about $94.1 million. Analyst and extrapolated estimates in the model indicate free cash flow reaching about $1.1 billion by 2030, with ten year projections moving from small losses in 2026 to forecasts in the hundreds of millions of dollars between 2027 and 2035.

Discounting all those projected cash flows back to today gives an estimated intrinsic value of about $665.53 per share. Compared with a recent share price around $178, the DCF output suggests the stock is 73.2% below that modelled value, which screens as significantly undervalued within this framework.

Result: UNDERVALUED

For companies that are still building toward steady profitability, the P/S ratio is often more useful than P/E or P/B, because it focuses on how much you are paying for each dollar of revenue rather than current earnings or book value.

In simple terms, higher growth expectations and lower perceived risk usually justify a higher “normal” P/S multiple, while slower growth or higher risk tend to support a lower one. That context matters when you look at Axsome Therapeutics today.

Axsome trades on a P/S of 14.27x, compared with a Pharmaceuticals industry average of 4.59x and a peer group average of 8.14x. Simply Wall St’s proprietary Fair Ratio for Axsome is 14.47x, which reflects factors such as its earnings growth profile, margins, industry, market cap and specific risks.

This Fair Ratio can be more informative than a simple comparison with peers or the wider industry because it is tailored to Axsome’s own characteristics rather than applying a broad sector multiple. With the current 14.27x P/S sitting very close to the 14.47x Fair Ratio, the shares appear roughly in line with what this framework would suggest.

title: Axsome Faces Key Auvelity FDA Call And Insider Sentiment Test
content:
Find winning stocks in any market cycle. Join 7 million investors using Simply Wall St's investing ideas for FREE.

Axsome Therapeutics (NasdaqGM:AXSM) is awaiting an FDA decision this month on Auvelity for agitation associated with Alzheimer's disease. The outcome could affect the potential reach of Auvelity within a large and currently underserved symptom area. Recent insider transactions reported in SEC filings show company executives actively trading Axsome shares.

Axsome Therapeutics approaches this FDA decision with its shares at $178.11 and a one-year return of 81.6%. Over the past three years, the stock has generated a 160.0% return and over five years, a 233.3% return, which may catch the eye of investors tracking longer-term performance. More recently, the shares show a 5.7% move over the past week and 14.1% over the past month, while year to date the stock is roughly flat at a 0.3% decline.

For readers assessing NasdaqGM:AXSM, the combination of an upcoming regulatory call on Auvelity and visible insider trading activity creates a clear focal point this month. The FDA outcome and any further disclosures around insider sentiment are likely to be key data points for how investors frame Axsome's risk and opportunity profile from here.

The upcoming FDA decision on Auvelity for agitation in Alzheimer’s disease sits at the center of how investors are reading Axsome right now, especially when viewed alongside the recent insider trades and supportive analyst sentiment. Open market purchases and sales under pre-approved plans signal that directors are actively managing exposure around a key binary event, rather than moving in a single clear direction. At the same time, several banks have reiterated positive ratings and raised price targets, which shows that professional coverage is treating the Auvelity filing and broader CNS portfolio as important drivers for the equity story. With a PDUFA date already set and a first quarter 2026 update scheduled soon after, you effectively have a cluster of information events that could reshape how the market prices Axsome’s risk and reward trade off in the near term.

How This Fits Into The Axsome Therapeutics Narrative

The Alzheimer’s agitation filing for Auvelity lines up with the narrative that Axsome is building a broader CNS portfolio, with new indications supporting a more diversified revenue base over time. Insider transactions and the regulatory uncertainty around the PDUFA decision highlight the dependence on a relatively narrow product set, which the narrative already flags as a key vulnerability. The pattern of insider trading around this catalyst, and any future trading after the decision, is not explicitly captured in the narrative and could add an extra layer of sentiment driven risk that investors weigh alongside the fundamental story.

Story Continues

The Risks and Rewards Investors Should Consider

⚠️ Heavy reliance on Auvelity and a small group of CNS assets means an unfavorable FDA outcome for the Alzheimer’s agitation indication could weigh on future revenue concentration and increase earnings volatility. ⚠️ Ongoing investment in commercial infrastructure, including a larger sales force and higher SG&A, could keep margins under pressure if product uptake or new indications do not track current expectations. 🎁 Analysts continue to issue positive ratings and higher targets, which points to a view that the existing portfolio and late-stage pipeline can support further business expansion if execution stays on track. 🎁 The Alzheimer’s agitation opportunity, if approved, would be incremental to current uses of Auvelity and could extend its reach into a large symptom area where treatment options have meaningful limitations.

What To Watch Going Forward

Over the next few weeks, the key items to watch are the FDA decision on Auvelity for Alzheimer’s agitation, any label details that could affect how physicians use the drug, and follow up commentary from management on the May 4 earnings call. Investors are also likely to pay attention to the size and direction of insider transactions after the decision, as well as any shifts in analyst ratings or price targets that incorporate updated assumptions for Auvelity and the rest of the CNS portfolio.

title: Is This Healthcare Stock a Millionaire Maker?
content:
Axsome Therapeutics(NASDAQ: AXSM), a midcap biotech, went public in 2015. Since then, the stock has delivered market-beating returns thanks to significant clinical and regulatory progress, as well as a portfolio of now-approved drugs that generate solid sales. Axsome Therapeutics might only be getting started. The company still has a deep pipeline and plenty of catalysts ahead. But does it have what it takes to turn average investors into millionaires?

Lots of moving parts

If you had invested $50,000 into Axsome Therapeutics following its IPO, you would be sitting on close to $1 million today, given its compound annual growth rate of 33.32% over this period. Can the biotech pull off a similar performance through the next decade? That's unlikely, as it would give the company a market cap of about $157 billion, making it one of the largest drugmakers in the world. It's not impossible, to be clear, but it's an incredibly high bar to expect Axsome Therapeutics to match the performance it has had since 2015, when it started as a significantly smaller biotech stock.

Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? Our team just released a report on the one little-known company, called an "Indispensable Monopoly" providing the critical technology Nvidia and Intel both need. Continue »Image source: Getty Images.

Could the biotech record the required returns through the next two or three decades to turn $50,000 into $1 million? Maybe, as Axsome Therapeutics has an attractive pipeline that could help it drive solid growth at least through the 2040s, when some of its most important current products will lose patent exclusivity. Consider Auvelity, a medicine for depression that is currently its most critical growth driver. In 2025, Axsome Therapeutics' revenue grew 66% year over year to $638.5 million, driven primarily by Auvelity.

The medicine could soon gain an important label expansion for the treatment of agitation in Alzheimer's disease (AD). This indication would add a large addressable market to an already strong franchise, given that there are more than five million AD patients who suffer from agitation in the U.S., and there are few treatment options. Auvelity should keep pulling Axsome Therapeutics' sales in the right direction for a long time.

Beyond this medicine, though, Axsome Therapeutics has a deep pipeline of phase 3 assets across several conditions. If it can launch these products in the next few years, the company will be able to target well over 150 million patients; Axsome Therapeutics predicts peak sales of over $16 billion for its current lineup.  That sounds great. However, investors should consider the risks.

Story Continues

Axsome Therapeutics has faced several regulatory setbacks before, and although it overcame them, similar challenges could sink the stock price and delay clinical or commercial progress in the future. Worse, some of its candidates may never earn approval. And over long periods of more than a decade, we should also consider the very real possibility that newer medicines will erode its market share, even without the company encountering patent cliffs.

To turn investors into millionaires in the next 30 years, Axsome Therapeutics will have to avoid or at least navigate these troubles while also constantly innovating and replenishing its pipeline. Although the healthcare company has performed well so far, its long-term outlook remains uncertain, given how much could go wrong if it fails to secure key clinical and regulatory wins over the next five years. That said, I think the stock is worth serious consideration. Interested investors might want to initiate a small position in the company and progressively adding to it as it strengthens its lineup.
